name: Do you need a permit to remove an in-ground pool in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do you need a permit for in-ground pool removal in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?
mainEntity.text: Do you need a permit for in-ground pool removal in Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, or Burbank?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permit requirements vary by city and by scope. A simple partial fill-in may still need approval if the work affects drainage, grading, retaining walls, utility lines, or engineered compaction. Full removals often trigger more review because the excavation and backfill process can change how the site drains and supports future use. In places like Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, and Burbank, the safest approach is to have the contractor verify local requirements before any demolition begins. Homeowners should ask who pulls the permit, whether engineering is needed, and what inspections are required before backfill and final grading. If the property is on a slope or near a hillside, permit scrutiny can be even higher. A contractor familiar with local rules can prevent costly rework and schedule delays.
acceptedAnswer.description: Most in-ground pool removals in Los Angeles County require permit review, especially when excavation, hauling, grading, drainage changes, or structural work are involved. Requirements can differ by city and by whether the project is a partial fill-in or full removal. Homeowners should confirm permit needs before demolition starts to avoid delays, inspection issues, and stop-work orders.
